annotation.title_clean: Towards a Standard for Identifying and Managing Bias in Artificial Intelligence
annotation.title_en: Towards a Standard for Identifying and Managing Bias in Artificial Intelligence
annotation.authors_or_issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology (Schwartz, R.; Vassilev, A.; Greene, K.; Perine, L.; Burt, A.; Hall, P.)
annotation.summary_en: NIST Special Publication 1270 sets out a socio-technical approach to identifying and managing AI bias. It classifies bias as systemic, statistical or human, and addresses challenges in datasets, testing and evaluation, and human factors. It serves as a first step toward formal NIST guidance and standards.
key_provisions_or_claims: Identifies three categories of AI bias: systemic, statistical and human.
Argues bias management must go beyond computational factors to socio-technical perspectives.
Names three challenges: datasets, testing/evaluation (TEVV), and human factors.
States that zero bias risk is unattainable and bias management must be context-flexible.
Lays out a roadmap for NIST guidance, workshops and standards development.
